title: Review of c16's evoloop (IBDH): reproduction and kind-level heredity replicate on fresh seed 5, but no small kind sweeps within 200k steps; Weak
summary: I looked at kinds.png, birthstrip_s2.png and pack/seed2/sheet.png, then ran the claimed world.py on seed 5 twice: a labkit pack (300^2, 20000 steps, lineage K=3 as in the claim) and the claim's evo_track.py tracker (400^2, founder m=15, 200000 steps; data/trk_s5.json.gz). labkit: 255 persistent splits, max generation 28, merge/split 0.38, sheathed square loops copying into same-size daughters (rerun/seed5/sheet.png), matching seeds 1-2. Tracker: 28417 births with a parent, 12956 off-kind daughters, 0.04 conversions of living loops per off-kind birth; the founders' side 11 breeds true 0.69 and side 12 0.68 (as claimed), and small kinds arise (sides 2-5), but on this seed they breed true only 0.02-0.68 (side 3: 0.14, side 4: 0.07) and never sweep: at t=200000 side 11 holds 54 of 63 loops, side 12 4 (kinds_s5.png). Side 5-6 loops have the highest births per loop-time (4.3-4.9 per 1000 vs 2.0 for side 11) but breed true only 0.02, so their daughters are other sizes. The claim's sweeps came at t~85k-190k on its 3 seeds, so a fourth seed without one by 200k says the replacement is not guaranteed in that window rather than contradicting it.

observations.B: rerun/seed5/sheet.png sheath channel around each loop (written by the rule)
observations.D: rerun/seed5/FACTS.md: 255 persistent splits, max generation 28, merge/split 0.38

seeds_run.result: pass for I, B, D; H not seen: no kind replaces the founders' side 11 within 200000 steps (54/63 loops at the end)

controls_run.H: none run by me; the claim's SDSR variation control was not re-run

verdicts.limitation: One fresh seed. Heredity of the founders' kinds replicates (side 11 and 12 breed true 0.69/0.68) but the selection result (small kinds displacing the founders) did not occur within 200000 steps on seed 5; small kinds there breed true poorly (0.07-0.14 for sides 3-4). Founders are planted (S fails), B is written by the rule, and there is no identical-event neutral twin.
